text: Benin City (Nigeria) was founded or first settled around 1180 CE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Benin: city walls mark growth 'from 850 AD'; Igodomigodo 'coalesced ... in the late 1st millennium CE'. 1180 looks like a dynasty date, not the city's start.
fix: Set start to about 900 with start_range [850, 1000]; keep 1180 as an event (Eweka dynasty).

text: Venice (Italy) was founded or first settled around 421 CE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Venice: traditional founding 'at the stroke of noon on 25 March 421' (a tradition, no surviving record).
fix: Mark it as the traditional date.

text: Mexico City (Mexico) was founded or first settled around 1325 CE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Tenochtitlan: 13 March 1325 is the conventional date, 'chosen in 1925' for the 600th anniversary; true date unclear.

text: Byblos (Lebanon) was founded or first settled around 5000 BCE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Byblos: 'first settled between 8800 and 7000 BC and continuously inhabited since 5000 BC'. 5000 BCE is the continuous-habitation date, not first settlement.
fix: Say 'continuously inhabited since 5000 BCE' or move start to -8800 with a range.

text: Ravenser Odd (UK (Humber estuary)) was founded or first settled around 1235 CE (approx.).
evidence: Wikipedia, Ravenser Odd: 'founded by the Count of Aumale in the mid-13th century'; borough charter 1 April 1299. No source found for exactly 1235.

text: Anuradhapura ended or was abandoned around 993 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Chola conquest of Anuradhapura: 'Rajaraja I invaded Anuradhapura sometime in 993 AD'; capital moved to Polonnaruwa.

text: Chan Chan ended or was abandoned around 1470 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Chan Chan: 'After the Inca conquered the Chimú around 1470 AD, Chan Chan fell into decline' (declined, not emptied at once).

text: Buddhas of Bamiyan ended or was abandoned around 2001 CE.
evidence: 9/11 Memorial: assault began 2 March 2001; 'By the end of March 2001, the Bamiyan Buddhas had been reduced to piles of rubble'.

text: Monte Albán ended or was abandoned around 850 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Monte Albán: lost political pre-eminence by c. 500-750; 'by the end of the same period (c. AD 900-1000), the ancient capital was largely abandoned'.

text: Beijing: Ji, then the Mongols' Dadu, then the Ming and Qing capital. Capital of China for most of the last 750 years; around 1800 perhaps the largest city on earth.
evidence: Wikipedia, largest cities in history: Beijing 1,100,000 in 1800 (Modelski, Chandler, Morris), the largest listed.

text: Hangzhou: Lin'an, the Southern Song capital at the end of the Grand Canal. Marco Polo called it the finest city in the world; possibly the world's largest around 1200.
evidence: Columbia Asia for Educators quotes Marco Polo: 'the finest and the noblest in the world'. Morris lists Hangzhou at 1,000,000 in 1200 (Modelski prefers Baghdad), so 'possibly' is fair.

sources.cite: Columbia Asia for Educators quotes Marco Polo

text: Medina: Yathrib, the oasis town where Muhammad moved in 622. The Hijra year 622 is year one of the Islamic calendar.
evidence: Wikipedia, Hijri era: the epoch 'is the year in which Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Yathrib' (622 CE).

text: Aachen: Charlemagne's favourite residence and burial place. German kings were crowned here for about 600 years.
evidence: Aachen Cathedral: 'Between 936 and 1531, the coronations of 30 kings and 12 queens ... took place in Aachen'; Charlemagne buried there.

text: Córdoba: Capital of the Umayyad caliphate of al-Andalus. Around 1000 perhaps the largest city in Europe, with a famous library and the Great Mosque.
evidence: Wikipedia, largest cities in history: Chandler puts Córdoba at 350,000 in 1000, the only European city in the top rows.

text: Berlin, 1871 CE: Capital of the German Empire.
evidence: Wikipedia, History of Berlin: 'the capital of the German Empire in 1871'.

text: Lisbon, 1497 CE: Da Gama sails for India.
evidence: Wikipedia (schools edition), Vasco da Gama: 'On 8 July 1497 the fleet, consisting of four ships, left Lisbon.'

text: Nanjing, 1421 CE: Ming court moves to Beijing.
evidence: Wikipedia, Yongle era: Beijing officially declared principal capital on 28 October 1420; government agencies had moved by February 1421.

text: Persepolis, 518 BCE: Darius I begins building.
evidence: World History Encyclopedia: 'Construction began between 518-515 BCE under Darius I.'

text: Tyre, 1291 CE: Taken by the Mamluks.
evidence: Wikipedia, Fall of Outremer: Tyre 'would remain in Christian hands until 1291', when the Mamluks took the last Crusader ports.

text: Teotihuacan, 200 CE: Pyramid of the Sun completed.
evidence: Wikipedia, Pyramid of the Sun: built about 200 AD; that first stage brought it 'to nearly the size it is today'; a second, undated stage completed it.

text: Delhi, 1206 CE: Delhi Sultanate founded.
evidence: Wikipedia, Mamluk dynasty (Delhi): established 1206.

text: Naples had about 280,000 people in 1600 CE.
evidence: T.A. Morris, Europe and England in the Sixteenth Century (1998), p.14: Naples 280,000 ca. 1600 (via U. Oregon course table).

sources.cite: T.A. Morris, Europe and England in the Sixteenth Century (1998), p.14

text: Damascus had about 90,000 people in 1200 CE.
evidence: No population figure for Damascus around 1200 found on Wikipedia (Damascus, Ayyubid dynasty) or in a wider search.

sources.cite: No population figure for Damascus around 1200 found on Wikipedia (Damascus, Ayyubid dynasty) or in a wider search.

fix: Find a source (e.g. Chandler 1987) or mark the point as a draft guess.

text: Bruges had about 46,000 people in 1340 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Bruges: 'grew to at least 46,000 inhabitants ... around 1350 AD'. Atlas says 1340; close enough.

text: Mexico City had about 200,000 people in 1500 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Tenochtitlan: 1519 estimates 200,000-400,000; 'most common estimates ... over 200,000'.

text: Fez had about 150,000 people in 1300 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia (Fez; History of Fez) gives 200,000 for the 12th century and nothing for 1300.

sources.cite: Wikipedia (Fez; History of Fez) gives 200,000 for the 12th century and nothing for 1300.

fix: Find a source for 1300 or use the 12th-century figure with its citation.

text: Egypt (New Kingdom) lasted from 1550 BCE to 1070 BCE.
evidence: Standard chronology: New Kingdom c. 1550-1069 BC (Wikipedia, New Kingdom of Egypt).

text: Khmer Empire lasted from 802 CE to 1431 CE.
evidence: Wikipedia, Khmer Empire: 'conventionally dated to 802 AD'; in 1431 Ponhea Yat abandoned Angkor.

text: Hittite Empire peaked around 1300 BCE at about 0.6 million km².
evidence: Wikipedia, List of largest empires (after Taagepera): New Kingdom Hittite 0.45 million km² in 1250-1220 BC. Atlas has 0.6, a third too high.

sources.cite: Wikipedia, List of largest empires (after Taagepera)

text: Ptolemaic Egypt peaked around 240 BCE at about 1 million km².
evidence: Wikipedia, List of largest empires: Ptolemaic Kingdom 1.0 million km², dated 301 BC. Area matches; peak year differs.
fix: Check Taagepera 1979 for the peak year.
